significance.justification: Verified true, the conclusion would be that fabricated assistant turns activate a distinct false-self-authorship signal that "scal[es] with shot count," is suppressed by other-attribution, and causally lowers refusal beyond attention diffusion and imitation; this combines a form-(iii) measurable ordering with a form-(ii) causal decomposition. It establishes both a phenomenon—authorship framing changes jailbreak susceptibility—and a mechanism that fixes predictions for shot count, attribution, model self-recognition, and bidirectional interventions, rather than merely identifying another refusal-related direction. Anthropic's Many-shot Jailbreaking (Anil et al., 2024, arXiv:2404.02151) makes the growth of attack efficacy with demonstrations an operational safety problem; a negative result here would still rule out self-authorship as its distinct explanation and redirect mechanistic work toward imitation or attention diffusion. True and false outcomes are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check lowers no score: replacing this account with the generic safety-interpretability topic would erase the specific authorship-versus-imitation decomposition and its scaling prediction.

reach.justification: The claim hands over two named handles: the "self-authorship projection" as an attack-success predictor and "Self-Authorship Neutralization (SAN)" as a training-free inference-time context filter. SAN is ex ante because it acts on injected context before the final response, giving model operators an opportunity to gate or neutralize a suspected fabricated history rather than merely explain a jailbreak afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the asserted monotonic relation among shot count, attribution framing, self-authorship signal, and compliance predicts what should recur across chat-tuned models, although the claim narrows likely applicability to "open 7-9B chat models" and acknowledges adaptive attackers, so it does not support universal deployment. The downstream users include researchers and practitioners who audit or ship chat systems, and the topic-substitution check supports the score because generic mechanistic safety alone supplies neither this pre-output filter nor its attribution-based design rule.
